Google Workspace

Work the way many offices, schools, and small businesses do every day: store and share files in Google Drive, write in Google Docs, track work in Google Sheets, present with Google Slides, and stay in touch with Gmail, Google Calendar, and Google Meet.

Google Workspace was called G Suite until October 2020. You may still hear people use the old name; it is the same set of apps.

Google Workspace vs Microsoft 365

If you know Word, Excel, or Outlook, you already know most of what these apps do. Here is how the two families line up.

Google Workspace apps and their Microsoft 365 equivalents
Google WorkspaceMicrosoft 365Used for
Google DriveOneDrive (and SharePoint for team files)Store, organize, and share files in the cloud
Google DocsWordLetters, notices, procedures, reports
Google SheetsExcelLists, logs, budgets, schedules, charts
Google SlidesPowerPointPresentations and training decks
GmailOutlook (mail)Email
Google CalendarOutlook (calendar)Meetings, appointments, shared calendars
Google Meet and Google ChatMicrosoft TeamsVideo meetings and team chat
Google FormsMicrosoft FormsSign-up forms, surveys, quizzes

It runs in the browser

Nothing to install. Sign in to your Google account in Chrome, Edge, Firefox, or Safari on any computer and your files are there.

There is no Save button

Docs, Sheets, and Slides save every change to Google Drive as you work. Version history keeps earlier versions you can go back to.

You share a link, not an attachment

Everyone works in the same file at the same time instead of emailing copies back and forth. You choose who can view, comment, or edit.

It still works with Office files

Drive opens Word, Excel, and PowerPoint files, and Docs, Sheets, and Slides download as .docx, .xlsx, and .pptx when someone needs an Office file.

Many workplaces use both. Learning the Google apps alongside the Microsoft Office courses means you can step into either kind of office.

Course Modules

Work through the modules in order, at your own pace. Each lesson has a slideshow, notes, a knowledge check, practice games, a practice simulation, and a challenge.

Module 1
🧭

Getting Started with Google Workspace

Learn what Google Workspace is, sign in safely, move between Drive, Docs, Sheets, and Slides, and work with the Microsoft Office files people send you.

🎓 Beginner⏱ 1h 20m📚 4 lessons
Module 2
📁

Google Drive: Organize and Share

Upload, organize, find, share, and recover files in Google Drive so the whole office can find the current version of anything in seconds.

🎓 Beginner⏱ 1h 35m📚 5 lessons
Module 3
📝

Google Docs

Write, format, structure, review, and send professional documents in Google Docs: notices, handbooks, updates, and letters.

🎓 Beginner⏱ 2h📚 5 lessons
Module 4
📊

Google Sheets

Enter and format data, calculate with formulas and functions, sort and filter, chart and summarize, and keep shared spreadsheets clean in Google Sheets.

🎓 Beginner to Intermediate⏱ 2h 15m📚 5 lessons
Module 5
🖼️

Google Slides

Build a clear presentation in Google Slides: themes and layouts, pictures and backgrounds, gentle motion and speaker notes, then present it, share it, and download PowerPoint and PDF copies.

🎓 Beginner⏱ 1h 20m📚 4 lessons
Module 6
✉️

Gmail

Run a work inbox in Gmail: sort and clean up mail, write and reply with the right recipients and files, schedule and protect messages, organize with labels and filters, and stay safe from phishing.

🎓 Beginner⏱ 1h 55m📚 5 lessons
Module 7
📅

Google Calendar & Google Meet

Plan the office's week in Google Calendar, invite people at times they're free, share calendars and booking pages, and take part in Google Meet calls with confidence.

🎓 Beginner⏱ 1h 30m📚 4 lessons
Module 8
🤝

Working Together

Work as a team in Google Workspace: quick conversations in Google Chat, comments and assigned action items in shared files, version history for team mistakes, and a small project that brings Gmail, Chat, Drive, Calendar, and Meet together.

🎓 Beginner⏱ 1h 5m📚 3 lessons

Before you start

  • • Basic computer and web browser skills.
  • • A free personal Google account is enough for every challenge. A work or school Google account works too, though your organization may turn some features off.
  • • The practice simulations run right on this site, with no account and nothing to install.
  • • The company, people, and records in this course are fictional. Never practice with real customer or personal information.
